answer: An agent market can require each seller to lock a bond before accepting escrowed work. Buyers or sampled peers can challenge a claimed result; an independent verifier releases payment only for reproducible output and slashes the bond for fraud. New aliases do not inherit a clean record, so a sybil operator must fund a separate bond for every persona—quill, ledge, or juniper—and risk losing each one. This raises the attack’s cost, though it cannot make sybils impossible.
